industries.name: Digital Technology & Software
industries.intro: Tech isn't one job — it's about eight different worlds under one roof. You can build software, run the systems behind it, work with data and AI, protect it, test it, design it, or work in tech without coding all day.
industries.one_thing: You don't have to code all day to be in tech. Some build the product, some run it, some work with data, and many shape it without writing code at all. Which pull is strongest — building, operating, data, or the people-and-product side?
industries.wont_give: Total stability or freedom from constant learning. Tools and frameworks change fast, layoffs cycle, and you must keep relearning. If you want a fixed skill set that stays still, this world will tire you.

families.name: Getting Into Tech — Support & IT
families.blurb: The most common no-degree on-ramp.

roles.name: IT Support / Help Desk
roles.description: Front-line tech help — fixing accounts, devices, access, and connectivity for an organization.
roles.reality: Often the role everyone only calls when something's broken; can be repetitive.
roles.day_to_day: Resetting accounts, fixing devices and connectivity, logging tickets, walking people through fixes.
roles.where_it_leads: Cybersecurity, cloud, sysadmin, or DevOps — the classic launchpad.
roles.needs: No degree required; CompTIA A+ / Google IT Support cert helps.

families.name: Building Software
families.blurb: The core — people who write the code that becomes apps, websites, and products.

roles.name: Frontend Developer
roles.description: Builds everything you see and touch — buttons, layouts, animations, the feel of a website or app.
roles.reality: Design and browsers fight you constantly; tools change fast.
roles.day_to_day: Turning designs into working screens, refreshing the browser, testing on phones and browsers.

roles.name: Backend Developer
roles.description: Builds the invisible engine — servers, databases, and the logic powering what users see.
roles.reality: Nobody notices when it works; everyone notices at 3am when it breaks.
roles.day_to_day: Writing server logic, handling data, logins, payments; fixing data flow issues.

roles.name: Full-Stack Developer
roles.description: Does both front and back. The startup default.
roles.reality: 'Knows everything' can mean 'master of nothing'; two moving worlds to track.
roles.day_to_day: Jumping between the user-facing screen and the engine behind it, often building a feature end to end.

roles.name: Mobile Developer
roles.description: Builds iOS and Android apps.
roles.reality: Apple and Google change rules yearly; app-store rejections stall work.

roles.name: Game Developer
roles.description: Builds interactive games — mechanics, physics, graphics.
roles.reality: Famous 'crunch' hours, lower pay, brutal competition.

families.name: Infrastructure & Operations
families.blurb: Keeping everything fast, online, and deployable.

roles.name: DevOps Engineer
roles.description: Automates how software gets tested, shipped, and deployed to millions.
roles.reality: You're on call; when the system goes down it's your night and weekend.

roles.name: Cloud / Site Reliability Engineer (SRE)
roles.description: Keeps massive systems running on AWS/Azure/Google Cloud.
roles.reality: Success is invisible — nobody thanks you for nothing breaking.

roles.name: Network / Systems Administrator
roles.description: Manages the servers, networks, and hardware an organization runs on.
roles.reality: Can feel like 'the IT person' everyone only calls when something's wrong.

families.name: Data & AI
families.blurb: The fastest-growing corner of tech.

roles.name: Data Analyst
roles.description: Turns raw data into clear answers — charts, reports, dashboards.
roles.reality: A lot of the job is cleaning messy data and chasing what people actually want.
roles.where_it_leads: Data scientist, analytics engineer, product analytics.
roles.needs: One of the most common no-CS-degree doors.

roles.name: Data Engineer
roles.description: Builds the pipes that move and store data reliably.
roles.reality: Invisible plumbing — vital, but upstream of the credit.

roles.name: Data Scientist
roles.description: Finds patterns and builds models that predict and explain.
roles.reality: Less glamorous than advertised — lots of data-wrangling first.

roles.name: Machine Learning / AI Engineer
roles.description: Builds and ships AI systems at scale.
roles.reality: Fast-moving and competitive; never stop learning.
roles.needs: Usually not a first job; strong CS/math base.

families.name: Security
families.blurb: Protecting systems from attack. Growing fast, pays well.

roles.name: Security Analyst
roles.description: Watches for threats, investigates alerts, keeps systems safe.
roles.reality: Quiet until it isn't — breaches bring intense pressure.
roles.needs: Reachable for career-changers via Security+ cert.

roles.name: Penetration Tester (Ethical Hacker)
roles.description: Legally breaks into systems to find holes before attackers do.
roles.reality: Glamorous-sounding, but methodical and report-heavy.

families.name: Quality & Testing
families.blurb: Making sure software works before it reaches users.

roles.name: QA / Test Engineer
roles.description: Tests software to catch bugs before users do.
roles.reality: Can be repetitive; sometimes seen as 'slowing the release'.
roles.needs: One of the easiest, most overlooked entries — great for career-changers; about being methodical, not highly technical.

roles.name: Automation Engineer (SDET)
roles.description: Writes code that tests other code automatically.
roles.reality: Sits between QA and dev; flaky tests are a constant headache.

families.name: In Tech, But Not Coding All Day
families.blurb: Deeply inside tech without writing code for eight hours.

roles.name: Product Manager
roles.description: Decides what a product should do and why, coordinating everyone to ship it.
roles.reality: Heavy responsibility, little direct authority.

roles.name: UX / UI Designer
roles.description: Designs how a product looks and feels.
roles.reality: Your work gets critiqued by everyone.

roles.name: Technical Writer
roles.description: Explains complex software clearly — guides, docs, API references.
roles.reality: Underrated and often understaffed.
roles.needs: A real door in for people from teaching/writing backgrounds.

roles.name: Solutions / Sales Engineer
roles.description: The technical expert in sales — shows customers how the product solves their problem.
roles.reality: You straddle sales targets and technical truth.

roles.name: Project / Program Manager & Scrum Master
roles.description: Keeps projects on track — timelines, blockers, delivery.
roles.reality: Accountable for delivery you don't directly control.

roles.name: Developer Advocate (DevRel)
roles.description: The bridge between a company and developers.
roles.reality: Part marketing, part engineering, belongs fully to neither.

roles.name: Business / Systems Analyst
roles.description: Translates business needs into clear requirements for the tech team.
roles.reality: Stuck in the middle; requirements never stop shifting.

families.name: Specializations — Emerging & Deep
families.blurb: Niche, deep corners you usually grow into.

roles.name: Embedded Systems Developer
roles.description: Codes the software inside physical devices — cars, appliances, medical gear, IoT.
roles.reality: Unforgiving — bugs can brick a device; hard hardware limits.

roles.name: Blockchain / Web3 Developer
roles.description: Builds decentralized apps and smart contracts.
roles.reality: Hype-prone and unstable; corners can collapse fast.

roles.name: AR / VR Developer
roles.description: Builds immersive augmented/virtual reality experiences.
roles.reality: Cutting-edge, still finding its market.

roles.name: Robotics Software Engineer
roles.description: Software for robots and autonomous systems.
roles.reality: Where software meets messy physical reality.

industries.name: Industrial Manufacturing & Automation
industries.intro: The world that physically makes things at scale — running factory floors, automating production, guarding quality, and keeping million-dollar machines alive. Three ways in: run the floor, automate it, or engineer the process.
industries.one_thing: Making real things, at scale. Do you want to run the floor and its people, automate the work with robots and systems, guard quality, keep the machines alive, or design the process itself?
industries.wont_give: Remote work, or freedom from shifts and location. It's tied to physical plants, shift-based, and often in industrial areas. If you need to work from anywhere, this isn't it.

families.name: Running the Floor
families.blurb: Turning a plant full of machines into finished product, on time and on budget.

roles.name: Production / Plant Manager
roles.description: Runs the entire factory floor — output, schedules, staff, safety, cost.
roles.reality: The buck stops with you when a line goes down; long hours, constant firefighting.

roles.name: Operations / Production Supervisor
roles.description: Runs a single shift or line — the bridge between floor workers and management.
roles.reality: Caught between management's targets and the crew's reality.
roles.needs: A common no-degree route up from the floor.

roles.name: Supply Chain / Materials Planner
roles.description: Makes sure the right materials arrive exactly when the line needs them.
roles.reality: Invisible when it works, blamed when one missing part halts a factory.

roles.name: EHS Specialist (Environment, Health & Safety)
roles.description: Ensures the factory doesn't hurt anyone or break environmental law.
roles.reality: Often seen as the 'police' by floor workers; needs thick skin.
roles.day_to_day: Safety audits, training staff on procedures, investigating incidents.

families.name: Automating the Work
families.blurb: The fastest-changing corner — replacing manual tasks with robots and smart systems.

roles.name: Automation / Controls Technician
roles.description: Installs, programs, and maintains the robots and control systems (PLCs) on automated lines.
roles.reality: When automation breaks, production stops and everyone watches you fix it.
roles.needs: Strong hands-on entry, often via a technical diploma.

roles.name: Robotics Integrator
roles.description: Designs and sets up entire automated cells — choosing and programming robots.
roles.reality: Projects are complex and deadline-driven; theory fails in messy reality.

families.name: Guarding Quality
families.blurb: Making sure what comes off the line is good — every unit.

roles.name: Quality Control Inspector / Analyst
roles.description: Tests and measures products against standards, catching defects.
roles.reality: You're the one slowing things down to reject bad product.
roles.needs: An accessible entry — methodical, not highly technical.

roles.name: Continuous Improvement / Lean Specialist
roles.description: Redesigns how the factory works to waste less time, money, material.
roles.reality: You ask people to change how they've always worked.

families.name: Keeping It Alive
families.blurb: The mechanics and problem-solvers who keep million-dollar machines turning on every day.

roles.name: Industrial Maintenance Technician
roles.description: Fixes what's broken and maintains what's running on the factory floor.
roles.reality: Physically demanding, dirty, high-pressure when a critical machine breaks — but massive job security.
roles.day_to_day: Tearing down pumps, wiring motors, replacing gears, preventative maintenance.
roles.where_it_leads: Maintenance supervisor, reliability engineering, field service.
roles.needs: One of the most accessible, highest-demand entries.

roles.name: Reliability Engineer
roles.description: Analyzes failure data to figure out why machines break and prevent it.
roles.reality: You must convince managers to spend on maintenance before things break — an uphill battle.
roles.needs: Usually a grow-into role, not a first job.

families.name: The Makers (Advanced Craft)
families.blurb: The modern artisans shaping metal and materials into precision parts.

roles.name: CNC Machinist
roles.description: Operates and programs computer-controlled machine tools that cut metal to precision.
roles.reality: One wrong line of code can crash a costly machine; intense focus.
roles.day_to_day: Reading blueprints, writing G-code, setting up stock, measuring to the thousandth.
roles.where_it_leads: Lead programmer, shop foreman, or own machine shop.

roles.name: Industrial Welder / Fabricator
roles.description: Fuses heavy metals to build structural components, piping, pressure vessels.
roles.reality: Heavy, hot, physically taxing — but skilled welders write their own ticket.

families.name: Designing the Process
families.blurb: The architects of efficiency — the best way to build the product.

roles.name: Manufacturing / Process Engineer
roles.description: Designs and optimizes the assembly line itself (vs. the product).
roles.reality: Caught in the middle: floor workers resist new processes, management resists budgets.

industries.name: Engineering & Applied Sciences
industries.intro: Engineering isn't one job — it's a way of thinking that lives inside almost every industry. The real choice isn't only 'what kind of engineer?' — it's 'which world do you want to engineer inside of?'
industries.one_thing: These foundations are roots, not endpoints. Engineering rewards people who'd rather be certain than fast. Pick the world that pulls at you; the right kind of engineering is already inside it.
industries.wont_give: Speed, low barriers, or constant reinvention. Engineering is credential-gated, regulation-heavy, and slow — because mistakes carry physical, sometimes life-or-death consequences. If you crave rapid iteration, Tech or Entrepreneurship fits better.

families.name: The Five Foundations
families.blurb: The trunk of the tree — pure disciplines you study first.

roles.name: Mechanical Engineering
roles.description: Anything that moves, has force, or involves heat/energy. The broadest foundation.

roles.name: Civil / Structural Engineering
roles.description: The built world: buildings, bridges, roads, water systems.
roles.needs: Accredited degree + PE license to sign off work.

roles.name: Electrical Engineering
roles.description: Electricity and electronics, from power grids to microchips.

roles.name: Chemical / Process Engineering
roles.description: Turning raw materials into products at scale: fuels, food, pharma.

roles.name: Materials Engineering / Metallurgy
roles.description: The substances things are made of: metals, polymers, composites.

roles.name: Computer / Hardware Engineer
roles.description: Designs the physical guts of computing: chips, boards, devices.
roles.reality: Long design cycles, expensive mistakes.

roles.name: Robotics / Mechatronics Engineer
roles.description: Blends mechanical, electrical, and software to build machines that sense and move.
roles.reality: Hardest part is where the three disciplines collide.

roles.name: Biomedical Engineer
roles.description: Designs medical devices, implants, diagnostic machines.
roles.reality: Regulation is slow and strict; approval can take years.

roles.name: Environmental Engineer
roles.description: Designs systems to clean water, cut pollution, manage waste.
roles.reality: Progress is slow and politics-bound.

roles.name: Renewable Energy / Grid Engineer
roles.description: Designs solar, wind, and the power grids that carry clean energy.
roles.reality: Fast-growing, but tied to policy and funding cycles.

roles.name: Industrial / Manufacturing Engineer
roles.description: Designs the factory and process that builds the product.
roles.reality: Caught between floor workers and management budgets.

roles.name: Automation Engineer
roles.description: Designs the automated systems and robotics that run modern production.
roles.reality: Complex, deadline-driven; real hardware rarely behaves like the plan.

roles.name: Agricultural / Biological Engineer
roles.description: Engineers the systems that grow and process food: machinery, irrigation, processing.
roles.reality: Tied to seasons, weather, and thin margins.

roles.name: Aerospace / Aeronautical Engineer
roles.description: Designs aircraft, spacecraft, and flight systems.
roles.reality: Extremely safety- and regulation-heavy; often security-cleared.

roles.name: Defense Systems / Nuclear Engineer
roles.description: Defense propulsion, national-lab work, and highly regulated power systems.
roles.reality: Among the most regulated, highest-clearance work there is.

roles.name: Petroleum / Mining Engineer
roles.description: Extracts oil, gas, and minerals from the earth at scale.
roles.reality: Boom-and-bust cycles, remote locations, growing climate scrutiny.

families.name: Specializations — Where Engineering Goes Deep
families.blurb: You grow into these after a core engineering degree.

roles.name: Geotechnical / Geological Engineer
roles.description: Evaluates soil, rock, and seismic faults so the ground can hold massive structures.
roles.day_to_day: Testing samples, modeling ground stability, advising on foundations.
roles.needs: Civil or Geological degree + PE license.

roles.name: Fire Protection / Safety Engineer
roles.description: Designs sprinklers, suppression, escape routes that protect life in buildings.
roles.needs: Fire Protection or Mechanical degree + PE license.

roles.name: Transportation / Traffic Engineer
roles.description: Designs highway interchanges, rail networks, runways.

roles.name: Water Resources / Hydraulic Engineer
roles.description: Designs dams, levees, flood defenses, water networks.
roles.needs: Civil or Environmental degree + PE license.

roles.name: Optical / Photonics Engineer
roles.description: Designs systems that manipulate light: lasers, lenses, fiber optics.
roles.needs: Optical Eng, Physics, or EE degree.

roles.name: Acoustical / Audio Engineer
roles.description: Controls sound and vibration: concert halls, quieting engines.

roles.name: Plastics / Polymer Engineer
roles.description: Engineers plastic compounds for high-stress uses.

roles.name: Ceramics & Glass Engineer
roles.description: Heat-resistant non-metallic solids, from heat shields to fiber optics.

roles.name: Food / Bioprocess Engineer
roles.description: Scales food/beverage production: pasteurization, fermentation.
roles.needs: Food, Chemical, or Biological Systems degree.

roles.name: Biochemical Engineer
roles.description: Scales vaccines, pharma, biofuels using living cells and bioreactors.

roles.name: Ergonomics / Human Factors Engineer
roles.description: Designs equipment to fit the human body's limits.
roles.needs: Industrial Eng, Biomechanics, or Kinesiology degree.

roles.name: Marine Engineer / Naval Architect
roles.description: Designs hulls and systems of ships, submarines, offshore platforms.
roles.needs: Marine Eng or Naval Architecture degree + maritime certs.

roles.name: Mining / Minerals Engineer
roles.description: Designs safe extraction: explosives, tunnel stability, ventilation.

roles.name: Textile / Garment Engineer
roles.description: Engineers synthetic fibers, smart fabrics, weaving machinery.
roles.needs: Textile Eng or Materials Science degree.

roles.name: Packaging Engineer
roles.description: Designs structural packaging that protects goods in shipping.

roles.name: Forensic Engineer
roles.description: Reverse-engineers collapses, fires, failures; expert witness in court.
roles.reality: A true grow-into — nobody starts here.
roles.needs: Core engineering degree + PE license + ~a decade of experience.

industries.name: Skilled Trades & Technical Craft
industries.intro: Work with your hands, see the result the same day, and get paid for genuine skill — not a paper credential. Demand is high, the work can't be offshored, and you can earn well without a four-year degree. Almost every trade is entered through an apprenticeship — you earn while you learn.
industries.one_thing: Tangible work, visible results, real skill. Power & systems, building & structure, metal & fabrication, vehicles & machines, or personal-service crafts — which kind of making appeals?
industries.wont_give: Desk comfort or freedom from physical wear. Trades are physical and take a toll on the body over decades; many involve weather, heights, or risk. If you want clean indoor desk work, look elsewhere.

families.name: Power & Systems
families.blurb: The invisible systems in every building and across the grid.

roles.name: Electrician
roles.description: Installs and maintains electrical systems.
roles.reality: Respected and well-paid, but mistakes can kill — code and precision matter.

roles.name: Plumber
roles.description: Installs and repairs water, gas, and drainage.
roles.reality: Recession-proof and high-paying; messy, physical, on-call.

roles.name: HVAC Technician
roles.description: Installs and services heating, cooling, ventilation.
roles.reality: Busy in extremes of heat/cold; part mechanic, part diagnostician.

roles.name: Refrigeration Technician
roles.description: Specialist in commercial/industrial cooling.
roles.reality: Niche, well-paid, urgent — spoiled stock means pressure.

roles.name: Power Line Worker (Lineman)
roles.description: Installs and repairs the power grid, often up poles or towers.
roles.reality: Genuinely dangerous, weather-exposed — and among the best-paid trades.

roles.name: Elevator / Escalator Mechanic
roles.description: Installs and services elevators and escalators.
roles.reality: One of the highest-paid trades; tightly licensed, hard to enter.

roles.name: Solar Panel Installer
roles.description: Installs rooftop and array solar systems.
roles.reality: Fast-growing with the energy shift; entry-friendly.

families.name: Building & Structure
families.blurb: Physically building and finishing spaces.

roles.name: Carpenter
roles.description: Builds with wood and framing.
roles.reality: Versatile and foundational; hard on the knees and back.

roles.name: Mason / Bricklayer / Concrete Worker
roles.description: Builds with brick, block, stone, concrete.
roles.reality: Heavy, physical, weather-dependent; lasting results.

roles.name: Roofer
roles.description: Installs and repairs roofs.
roles.reality: Tough, hot, high-risk; steady demand.

roles.name: Drywaller / Plasterer
roles.description: Hangs and finishes interior walls.
roles.reality: Dusty, repetitive, but quick visible results.

roles.name: Painter & Decorator
roles.description: Finishes surfaces.
roles.reality: Low entry barrier, easy to start solo; competitive.

roles.name: Flooring / Tile Installer
roles.description: Lays floors and tile.
roles.reality: Precise, hard on knees; craftsmanship rewarded.

roles.name: Glazier
roles.description: Installs glass and glazing.
roles.reality: Precise and physical; commercial work pays well.

roles.name: Insulation Installer
roles.description: Fits thermal/acoustic insulation.
roles.reality: Itchy, tight spaces; steady with energy-efficiency push.

roles.name: Heavy Equipment Operator
roles.description: Runs excavators, cranes, loaders.
roles.reality: Well-paid, weather-exposed, early starts.

families.name: Metal & Fabrication
families.blurb: Joining, shaping, and erecting metal.

roles.name: Welder
roles.description: Fuses metal.
roles.reality: Hot, physical; skilled welders travel and earn well.

roles.name: CNC Machinist
roles.description: Operates and programs computer-controlled tools that cut metal to precision.
roles.reality: One bad line can crash a costly machine — intense focus.

roles.name: Sheet Metal Worker / Fabricator
roles.description: Shapes and assembles sheet metal (ducts, panels).
roles.reality: Precise, hands-on; strong in HVAC/construction.

roles.name: Millwright
roles.description: Installs and maintains heavy industrial machinery.
roles.reality: Highly skilled, well-paid; demanding.

roles.name: Boilermaker
roles.description: Builds and repairs boilers, tanks, pressure vessels.
roles.reality: Physically brutal, often travel; excellent pay.

roles.name: Ironworker
roles.description: Erects structural steel for buildings and bridges.
roles.reality: One of the most dangerous trades; pays accordingly.

families.name: Mechanical & Vehicles
families.blurb: Keeping machines and vehicles running.

roles.name: Automotive Technician / Mechanic
roles.description: Diagnoses and repairs cars.
roles.reality: Ever more electronic; constant learning.

roles.name: Diesel / Heavy Vehicle Mechanic
roles.description: Services trucks, buses, heavy equipment.
roles.reality: Physical, well-paid, in-demand.

roles.name: Aircraft / Industrial Maintenance Technician
roles.description: Maintains aircraft or industrial machinery.
roles.reality: Heavily regulated, high-stakes, well-paid.

roles.name: Marine / Boat Mechanic
roles.description: Services boat and marine engines.
roles.reality: Niche, seasonal, location-bound.

roles.name: Small Engine / Motorcycle Technician
roles.description: Repairs bikes, mowers, small engines.
roles.reality: Lower pay, but easy to start solo.

roles.name: Appliance Repair Technician
roles.description: Fixes home and commercial appliances.
roles.reality: Steady, customer-facing; easy to go independent.

families.name: Personal & Service Trades
families.blurb: Crafts focused on people and places — often the fastest path to your own business.

roles.name: Chef / Professional Cook
roles.description: Prepares food professionally.
roles.reality: Low starting pay, intense hours; passion-driven.

roles.name: Barber / Hairstylist / Cosmetologist
roles.description: Cutting, styling, beauty services.
roles.reality: Builds a loyal book; income scales with reputation.

roles.name: Tattoo Artist
roles.description: Permanent body art.
roles.reality: Apprentice-based, reputation-driven, competitive.

roles.name: Locksmith
roles.description: Installs and repairs locks and security.
roles.reality: Niche, trust-based, easy to go solo.

roles.name: Landscaper / Arborist
roles.description: Shapes outdoor spaces; tree care.
roles.reality: Outdoor, seasonal; arborist work is high-risk/high-skill.

roles.name: Pest Control Technician
roles.description: Manages pests safely.
roles.reality: Steady, licensed, customer-facing.

families.name: Specializations — Where Trades Go Deep
families.blurb: Grow into these after mastering a core trade — niche, demanding, often spectacularly paid.

roles.name: Underwater Welder
roles.description: Welds underwater on rigs, pipelines, ships.
roles.reality: Dangerous, elite, among the highest-paid anywhere.

roles.name: Wind Turbine Technician
roles.description: Services wind turbines hundreds of feet up.
roles.reality: Fast-growing, high, weather-exposed.

roles.name: Telecommunications / Fiber Technician
roles.description: Installs and maintains fiber, cable, network infrastructure.
roles.reality: Growing with connectivity demand; trade + tech mix.

roles.name: Crane Operator (Tower/Mobile)
roles.description: Operates the largest lifting equipment on major sites.
roles.reality: Premium pay, heavy responsibility, certified.

roles.name: Instrumentation & Controls Technician
roles.description: Calibrates the sensors and control systems in industrial plants.
roles.reality: High-skill, well-paid; trade + electronics.

industries.name: Finance & Insurance
industries.intro: The world that moves money — pricing assets, funding companies, trading markets, and keeping the financial system running. It spans the glamorous and the essential-but-quiet, and pays among the highest of any field. In India, the doors run through credentials: B.Com/BBA as a base, then CA, CFA, FRM, NISM, or actuarial exams.
industries.one_thing: Money, markets, and measurable results. Deep analysis (investing, research), detail and rigor (accounting, audit), relationships (advice, banking), or the tech frontier (fintech, quant)?
industries.wont_give: Easy entry without credentials, or freedom from pressure. Many roles need hard exams (CA, CFA, FRM, actuarial) and the hours can be brutal. If you want a credential-light, low-stress path, look elsewhere.

families.name: Investment & Markets
families.blurb: The high-stakes core — mostly roles you grow into, not first jobs.

roles.name: Investment Banking Analyst
roles.description: Helps companies raise money, merge, or go public.
roles.reality: Intense hours, sharp feedback — but the fastest skill-builder in finance.
roles.needs: Top MBA (IIM/ISB) or CA; bulge-bracket roles fiercely selective.

roles.name: Trader
roles.description: Buys and sells assets for a firm.
roles.reality: High-stress, high-reward; not an entry seat.

roles.name: Sales & Trading (Markets Sales)
roles.description: Connects clients to market products.
roles.reality: Reads markets, manages relationships under pressure.

roles.name: Portfolio / Asset Manager
roles.description: Manages investment funds.
roles.reality: You grow into this after years of research.
roles.needs: CFA increasingly the standard for buy-side seats.

roles.name: Hedge Fund Analyst / Manager
roles.description: Aggressive, high-conviction investing.
roles.reality: Elite, hard to enter, performance-brutal.

roles.name: Equity / Investment Research Analyst
roles.description: Studies companies and recommends buy/sell.
roles.reality: Deep analytical work; India increasingly accepts strong self-taught profiles.

roles.name: Private Equity / Venture Capital Investor
roles.description: Invests in private companies and startups.
roles.reality: Prestigious exit from banking/consulting, rarely a first job.

roles.name: Investor Relations
roles.description: Bridges a company and its investors.
roles.reality: Disclosure-heavy, communication-driven.

families.name: Corporate & Accounting
families.blurb: The financial backbone of every company — India's most credential-defined corner.

roles.name: Bookkeeper / Accounting Associate
roles.description: Records daily transactions.
roles.reality: A genuine entry door; steady, detail-heavy.

roles.name: Accountant / Auditor
roles.description: Keeps books accurate and compliant.
roles.reality: The path to Controller and CFO.
roles.needs: CA (ICAI) is the gold standard; ACCA also recognised.

roles.name: Internal Auditor
roles.description: Checks a company's own controls and processes.
roles.reality: Process-focused, independent.

roles.name: Forensic Accountant
roles.description: Investigates fraud and financial crime.
roles.reality: Tracing money, sometimes testifying.

roles.name: Financial Analyst (FP&A)
roles.description: Plans and forecasts company finances.
roles.reality: A strong, common entry analytical role.

roles.name: Treasury Analyst / Manager
roles.description: Manages company cash, funding, and currency.
roles.reality: Liquidity, banking relationships, hedging.

roles.name: Tax Advisor / Specialist
roles.description: Plans and files taxes, navigates tax law.
roles.reality: Detail- and rule-heavy.

roles.name: Controller / CFO Track
roles.description: Runs all of a company's finance.
roles.reality: Senior leadership you climb to over 15+ years.
roles.needs: CA is the strongest credential for this track.

families.name: Risk, Insurance & Valuation
families.blurb: The science of pricing uncertainty.

roles.name: Actuary
roles.description: Prices long-term risk with heavy math.
roles.reality: Among the hardest exam paths anywhere; highly paid and secure.
roles.needs: Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI) exams from bachelor's — a long road.

roles.name: Risk Manager / Analyst
roles.description: Identifies and controls financial risk.
roles.reality: Modeling exposure, monitoring limits.
roles.needs: FRM (GARP) is the standard — preferred by HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak.

roles.name: Underwriter
roles.description: Decides whether to insure and at what price.
roles.reality: Assessing and pricing risk.

roles.name: Claims Analyst / Adjuster
roles.description: Investigates and settles insurance claims.
roles.reality: A real insurance entry door; detail- and judgment-heavy.

roles.name: Appraiser / Valuer
roles.description: Determines what assets are worth.
roles.reality: Inspecting and valuing assets.
roles.needs: Registered valuer credential for many uses.

roles.name: Insurance Agent / Broker
roles.description: Sells and advises on insurance.
roles.reality: Building a book of clients.

families.name: Banking Operations & Compliance
families.blurb: The machinery and guardrails — often the most realistic first job in finance.

roles.name: Loan Officer / Credit Analyst
roles.description: Assesses who gets credit.
roles.reality: A common bank entry role.

roles.name: Compliance Officer
roles.description: Keeps the firm within the rules.
roles.reality: Checking processes, flagging issues.

roles.name: AML / Financial Crime Analyst
roles.description: Hunts money laundering and fraud.
roles.reality: Fast-growing, investigative; a strong modern door.

roles.name: Settlements / Operations Analyst
roles.description: The back-office engine that settles trades.
roles.reality: One of the most realistic first jobs; banks and global back-offices hire heavily.

families.name: Advice & Client-Facing
families.blurb: Finance built on relationships.

roles.name: Financial Advisor / Wealth Manager
roles.description: Guides individuals' money and investments.
roles.reality: Trust-based, relationship-driven.
roles.needs: SEBI RIA needs NISM Investment Adviser exam + qualifying degree; CFP recognised.

roles.name: Commercial / Retail Banker
roles.description: Serves business or personal banking clients.
roles.reality: Relationships, loans, accounts.

families.name: FinTech & Modern Finance
families.blurb: Where finance meets technology — the fastest-growing frontier.

roles.name: Quantitative Analyst ('Quant')
roles.description: Builds math/code models for trading and risk.
roles.reality: Elite, code-heavy.

roles.name: Financial Data Analyst
roles.description: Uses data to optimize financial services.
roles.reality: A strong modern entry door; self-taught profiles increasingly accepted.

roles.name: FinTech Product Specialist
roles.description: Shapes digital financial products.
roles.reality: Works with engineers and users.

roles.name: Payments Specialist
roles.description: Works on how money moves digitally (UPI, cards, rails).
roles.reality: Huge in India given UPI's scale.

roles.name: Crypto / Blockchain Analyst
roles.description: Analyzes digital assets and blockchain.
roles.reality: Volatile, fast-moving, regulation-uncertain in India.

families.name: Specializations — Where Finance Goes Deep
families.blurb: Niche, high-skill paths you grow into.

roles.name: ESG / Sustainable Finance Analyst
roles.description: Aligns investments and reporting with ESG standards.
roles.reality: Fast-growing as ESG reporting becomes mandatory.

roles.name: Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) Specialist
roles.description: Lives in buying and selling companies.
roles.reality: Grows from investment banking.

roles.name: Restructuring / Distressed Specialist
roles.description: Rescues or unwinds troubled companies.
roles.reality: Grows from IB/credit.

roles.name: Catastrophe (CAT) Modeler
roles.description: Models extreme insurance risks — disasters, climate.
roles.reality: Grows from actuarial/risk.

roles.name: Treasury / Capital Markets Specialist
roles.description: Deep specialist in corporate funding and instruments.

industries.name: Economics
industries.intro: The study of how people, markets, and societies make choices under scarcity — why prices move, how economies grow, what policy does. Not finance (managing money) and not pure math — the lens that explains the forces behind both. Honest note: one of the most education-gated fields there is.
industries.one_thing: Understanding WHY the world works the way it does. Applied (business, markets), public (policy, central banks), data (econometrics), global (institutions), or research (academic)?
industries.wont_give: A fast, self-taught, no-degree shortcut. Economics is academic at its root; the doors open through formal study and strong quantitative skill. If you want hands-on, credential-light work, Trades or Tech fits better.

families.name: Applied & Business Economics
families.blurb: Economists working inside companies and markets.

roles.name: Business / Corporate Economist
roles.description: Advises a company on the economic forces shaping its market.
roles.reality: You inform decisions you don't make.

roles.name: Financial / Markets Economist
roles.description: Forecasts the economy, rates, and markets to guide investment.
roles.reality: Modeling trends, writing outlooks.
roles.needs: Economics degree → master's; CFA helps in India.

roles.name: Consulting Economist
roles.description: Brings economic analysis to client problems.
roles.reality: Building economic cases.
roles.needs: Strong econ degree → master's/PhD for senior work.

roles.name: Pricing / Revenue Economist
roles.description: Uses economic theory to set optimal prices.
roles.reality: A growing, very employable applied niche.

families.name: Public & Policy Economics
families.blurb: Economists who shape how a country runs.

roles.name: Policy Economist
roles.description: Analyzes and designs economic policy for government.
roles.reality: Studying impacts, advising officials.

roles.name: Central Bank Economist (e.g. RBI)
roles.description: Works on monetary policy, inflation, financial stability.
roles.reality: Prestigious, influential, competitive.
roles.needs: Master's/PhD; in India, RBI Grade B exam route.

roles.name: Development Economist
roles.description: Studies poverty, growth, and how economies develop.
roles.reality: Field research, program evaluation.

roles.name: Labour / Health / Education Economist
roles.description: Specializes in one sector's economics.
roles.reality: Sector policy research.

families.name: Data & Quantitative Economics
families.blurb: Where economics meets heavy data and code.

roles.name: Econometrician
roles.description: Builds statistical models to test economic theories with real data.
roles.reality: Rigorous, math-heavy, in demand.

roles.name: Economic Data Analyst
roles.description: Analyzes economic data for insights.
roles.reality: The closest economics has to an entry-level door.
roles.needs: Econ or data degree + strong data skills.

roles.name: Quantitative Economist
roles.description: Blends economics, statistics, and programming for forecasting.

roles.name: Economic Modeler
roles.description: Builds large simulations of economies or markets.

families.name: Global & Institutional Economics
families.blurb: Economics at the scale of nations and the planet.

roles.name: International Trade Economist
roles.description: Studies trade flows, tariffs, globalization.

roles.name: Economist at Global Bodies (World Bank, IMF, UN, ADB)
roles.description: Shapes economic policy across countries.
roles.reality: Elite, highly credentialed.

roles.name: Environmental / Climate Economist
roles.description: Prices the economics of climate, resources, and policy.
roles.reality: Fast-growing field.

roles.name: Agricultural Economist
roles.description: Economics of food, farming, and rural development.

families.name: Research & Academic Economics
families.blurb: Producing and teaching economic knowledge itself.

roles.name: Academic Economist / Professor
roles.description: Researches and teaches economics at a university.
roles.reality: A long PhD road; the deepest version of the field.

roles.name: Think-Tank Researcher
roles.description: Produces economic research to influence public debate.

roles.name: Behavioral Economist
roles.description: Studies how people actually decide vs. theory.
roles.reality: A growing crossover with psychology.

roles.name: Economic Journalist / Commentator
roles.description: Explains economics to the public.
roles.reality: Values communication over credentials — open to strong self-made writers.

families.name: Specializations — Where Economics Goes Deep
families.blurb: Niche fields you grow into through advanced study.

roles.name: Game Theorist
roles.description: Models strategic decision-making.

roles.name: Monetary Economist
roles.description: Deep specialist in money, banking, inflation.

roles.name: Public Finance Economist
roles.description: Specialist in taxation and government spending.

roles.name: Industrial Organization Economist
roles.description: Studies how industries and competition work.

industries.name: Entrepreneurship, Innovation & Consulting
industries.intro: Less a set of job titles and more a way of working — building, advising, and betting under uncertainty, where you own the outcome rather than a task. The highest autonomy and upside of any world, and the least security. Almost nothing here is degree-gated — the path in is usually to learn a craft first, then build.
industries.one_thing: A relationship with risk and ownership. Go all-in (founder, creator), sell your expertise (consulting, freelancing), build inside safety (intrapreneur, product), or back the builders (VC, operator)?
industries.wont_give: Security and predictability. No steady paycheck and a real chance of failure — income can be zero for long stretches. If you need stability to do your best work, an established world serves you better — and there's no shame in that.

families.name: Building Ventures
families.blurb: Creating something from nothing and owning the result.

roles.name: Startup Founder
roles.description: Builds a scalable company from an idea.
roles.reality: Most startups fail; years of uncertainty for a shot at the upside.
roles.day_to_day: Selling, hiring, fundraising, fixing whatever's broken — every hat.

roles.name: Small Business Owner
roles.description: Runs an established-model local business.
roles.reality: Steadier than a startup but relentless; you are the business.

roles.name: Solopreneur / Creator
roles.description: Builds a one-person business around a skill or audience.
roles.reality: Full freedom, full responsibility; income is lumpy.

roles.name: Freelancer / Independent Contractor
roles.description: Sells a skill (design, writing, code) to clients project by project.
roles.reality: The most common real entry into working for yourself — start while employed.

roles.name: E-commerce / Online Store Owner
roles.description: Sells products online (D2C, marketplace, dropshipping).
roles.reality: Low barrier to start, crowded and margin-tight to win.

roles.name: Content Creator / Audience Business
roles.description: Builds an audience and turns it into income.
roles.reality: Huge upside, brutal consistency required; most don't reach scale.

roles.name: Real Estate Developer / Investor
roles.description: Builds or invests in property for returns.
roles.reality: Capital-heavy and cyclical; leverage cuts both ways.

roles.name: Franchisee
roles.description: Runs a proven brand's outlet under license.
roles.reality: Lower risk than going solo, but fees and rules constrain you.

families.name: Expertise Businesses
families.blurb: Building a business out of selling expertise.

roles.name: Independent / Boutique Consultant
roles.description: Sells advice and problem-solving in a domain you've mastered.
roles.reality: You eat what you kill; reputation is everything.

roles.name: Agency Owner / Operator
roles.description: Builds a team that delivers a service to clients.
roles.reality: You graduate from doing the work to running people and sales.

families.name: Innovation Inside Organizations
families.blurb: Entrepreneurial upside without betting the house.

roles.name: Intrapreneur / New Ventures Lead
roles.description: Builds new products or business lines inside a company.
roles.reality: Startup energy with a salary — but corporate gravity slows you.

roles.name: Product Manager
roles.description: Decides what a product should do and rallies the team to ship it.
roles.reality: Own the outcome, can't command the team.

roles.name: Business Development / Growth Lead
roles.description: Finds and builds the deals and channels that grow a company.
roles.reality: Partnerships, deals, growth experiments.

roles.name: Corporate Strategist
roles.description: Shapes where a company should place its bets.
roles.reality: Market analysis, planning, advising leadership.

families.name: Backing & Enabling Ventures
families.blurb: Fund, guide, or enable builders.

roles.name: Venture Capitalist / Angel Investor
roles.description: Funds startups in exchange for equity.
roles.reality: Usually reached after operating or wealth; patient, high-risk bets.

roles.name: Startup Operator (Early Employee)
roles.description: Joins a young startup as an early hire and helps build it.
roles.reality: Less risk than founding, real upside, great learning.

roles.name: Incubator / Accelerator Manager
roles.description: Runs programs that help many startups grow.
roles.reality: Selecting and mentoring founders.

families.name: Specializations — Niche Venture Paths
families.blurb: Less common ways of owning and building.

roles.name: Social Entrepreneur
roles.description: Builds a venture to solve a social/environmental problem sustainably.
roles.reality: Balancing mission and money.

roles.name: Search-Fund / Acquisition Entrepreneur
roles.description: Raises money to buy an existing business and run it.
roles.reality: Hunting, financing, then operating.

roles.name: Family Business Successor
roles.description: Takes over and evolves a family enterprise.
roles.reality: Modernizing while managing family dynamics.

roles.name: Productized-Service Founder
roles.description: Turns a service into a repeatable product.
roles.reality: Systematizing delivery to scale beyond your hours.

roles.name: Indie Hacker / Micro-SaaS Founder
roles.description: Builds small software products solo for recurring revenue.
roles.reality: Coding, launching, marketing small tools to a niche.

industries.name: Healthcare, Longevity & Healing Sciences
industries.intro: The world built around health, healing, and the human body. Deeply meaningful and among the most secure work there is — but with the longest, most expensive training ladders and real emotional weight. Markers matter here: 🟢 learnable, 🟡 course/credential, 🔴 accredited degree + licence (signpost only).
industries.one_thing: Caring for and healing people. The clinical core needs long accredited training; the support and operations side has genuine accessible doors. Do you want to treat, to support, to research, or to run the systems?
industries.wont_give: Quick entry to the clinical core, or freedom from emotional weight. Most clinical roles need years of accredited study and licensing, and the work carries real emotional load and burnout. If you need fast entry, look to the support roles or another world.

roles.name: Physician / Surgeon
roles.description: Diagnoses and treats; surgeons operate.
roles.reality: The longest, hardest training ladder; immense responsibility.
roles.needs: MBBS + MD/MS + NMC registration; a decade+.

roles.name: GP / Family Doctor
roles.description: First point of care across all of life's stages.
roles.reality: Back-to-back consultations.

roles.name: Psychiatrist
roles.description: A medical doctor treating mental illness (can prescribe).
roles.reality: Assessments, medication management, therapy.

roles.name: Specialist Physician
roles.description: Deep expert in one system (cardiology, etc.).

roles.name: Registered Nurse
roles.description: The backbone of patient care.
roles.reality: Administering care and meds, monitoring patients.
roles.needs: B.Sc/GNM Nursing + Indian Nursing Council registration.

roles.name: Nurse Practitioner / Advanced Practice Nurse
roles.description: Senior nurse with expanded authority.
roles.reality: A grow-into role.

roles.name: Paramedic / EMT
roles.description: Emergency pre-hospital care.
roles.reality: High-adrenaline, life-and-death, irregular hours.

roles.name: Healthcare Assistant / Caregiver
roles.description: Hands-on daily support for patients and the elderly.
roles.reality: Emotionally meaningful, physically demanding, often underpaid — but a real door in.
roles.needs: Short caregiving courses; among the most accessible healthcare entries.

roles.name: Psychologist / Psychotherapist
roles.description: Treats mental health through talk therapy.
roles.reality: Deep, demanding emotional work.
roles.needs: Master's/doctoral psychology + RCI registration for clinical practice.

roles.name: Physical Therapist
roles.description: Restores movement after injury or illness.

roles.name: Occupational / Speech Therapist
roles.description: Rebuilds daily-living and communication skills.

roles.name: Clinical Counselor / Social Worker
roles.description: Supports people through crisis and life challenges.
roles.reality: More reachable than clinical psychology.

roles.name: Pharmacist
roles.description: Dispenses medication and advises on safe use.

roles.name: Radiographer / Imaging Technologist
roles.description: Operates X-ray, MRI, CT.
roles.reality: A reachable technical route.

roles.name: Medical Laboratory Scientist
roles.description: Runs the tests behind diagnoses.

roles.name: Dietitian / Nutritionist
roles.description: Guides health through food and nutrition.
roles.reality: Clinical needs a degree; wellness coaching is more open.

roles.name: Optometrist / Dentist / Audiologist
roles.description: Independent specialist practitioners (eyes, teeth, hearing).

roles.name: Epidemiologist
roles.description: Studies how disease spreads across populations.

roles.name: Public Health Official / Administrator
roles.description: Runs health programs and systems.

roles.name: Health Informatics Specialist
roles.description: Bridges healthcare and data/IT systems.
roles.reality: A fast-growing crossover where tech skills open the door.

roles.name: Hospital / Healthcare Administrator
roles.description: Runs the business and operations of a medical facility.
roles.reality: Budgets, compliance, patient flow.

families.name: Health Support & Operations
families.blurb: The accessible doors — often short-course, remote-friendly, the most realistic entry for career-changers.

roles.name: Medical Coder / Biller
roles.description: Translates diagnoses and procedures into standardized codes.
roles.reality: One of the best fits for self-directed learning — strong national + international remote demand.

roles.name: Phlebotomist
roles.description: Draws blood for tests and donation.
roles.reality: Short training, hands-on, a quick clinical-support entry.

roles.name: Pharmacy Technician
roles.description: Supports pharmacists dispensing medication.

roles.name: Medical Assistant
roles.description: Versatile clinic support (admin + basic clinical).
roles.reality: A broad, accessible foot-in-the-door role.

roles.name: Medical Scribe / Medical Writer
roles.description: Documents clinical encounters, or writes medical/health content.
roles.reality: Medical writing is genuinely self-learnable for strong writers.
roles.needs: Scribe training (short) or self-built medical-writing skill.

families.name: Specializations — Where Healthcare Goes Deep
families.blurb: Niche, advanced paths and emerging frontiers.

roles.name: Genetic Counselor
roles.description: Guides patients through genetic risk and testing.

roles.name: Clinical Research Associate
roles.description: Runs the trials that test new treatments.

roles.name: Clinical Trial Manager / Coordinator
roles.description: Manages the logistics of drug trials.
roles.reality: Recruiting patients, ensuring compliance, managing data.

roles.name: Medical Device / Health-Tech Specialist
roles.description: Works at the device/software edge of care.

roles.name: Health Coach / Wellness Practitioner
roles.description: Guides lifestyle, fitness, and preventive health.
roles.reality: Largely unregulated wellness space — accessible, but credibility varies.

roles.name: Biogerontologist / Longevity Researcher
roles.description: Studies the biology of aging to slow or reverse it.
roles.reality: Cutting-edge but a very small, deeply credentialed research niche.

roles.name: Regenerative / Recovery Therapy Technician
roles.description: Operates technology in stem-cell, hyperbaric, and recovery clinics.
roles.reality: An emerging, lightly-regulated space — legitimacy varies widely; research employers carefully.

roles.name: Perfusionist / Anesthesia Technologist
roles.description: Highly specialized surgical-support roles.

families.name: Integrative & Traditional Medicine
families.blurb: Parallel to allopathic medicine, not a sub-type — necessary in the Indian context.

roles.name: Traditional Medicine Practitioner (Ayurveda / Homeopathy / Unani / Siddha)
roles.description: Diagnoses and treats using established traditional systems.
roles.reality: A fully licensed, large profession in India.
roles.needs: Accredited degree (BAMS, BHMS, BUMS) + AYUSH/state council registration.

roles.name: Integrative / Alternative Therapist (Acupuncture / Chiropractic / Osteopathy)
roles.description: Physical and energy-based therapies.
roles.reality: Regulation varies a lot by region and modality.
roles.needs: Specialized degree or extensive diploma, depending on region.

industries.name: Academics, Education & Scientific Research
industries.intro: The world of knowledge — teaching it, discovering it, preserving it. Two opposite callings live here: the teacher who lights up in front of people, and the researcher who lives for the deep question. Many enter expecting one and discover they wanted the other.
industries.one_thing: Working with knowledge. Teaching and shaping people, discovering new knowledge through research, stewarding and organizing it, or the modern accessible side — training, edtech, course creation?
industries.wont_give: Quick rewards or, in research, security. The research track needs the most education (PhD) for some of the least security — years of low-paid postdocs chasing scarce permanent jobs. Teaching can be stable but rarely highly paid.

roles.name: School Teacher
roles.description: Teaches children or teens a subject or grade.
roles.reality: Planning, teaching, grading, managing a classroom.
roles.needs: Degree + B.Ed / teaching qualification (India: often TET).

roles.name: University Lecturer / Professor (teaching)
roles.description: Teaches at higher-ed level.

roles.name: Special Education Teacher
roles.description: Teaches students with special needs.
roles.reality: Individualized teaching, working with families.
roles.needs: Degree + special-ed qualification (RCI registration in India).

roles.name: Corporate Trainer / Instructional Designer
roles.description: Builds and delivers training for organizations.
roles.reality: A strong, self-learnable path that doesn't need a teaching degree.

roles.name: Tutor / Private Educator
roles.description: Teaches one-to-one or small groups.
roles.reality: One of the most accessible paths anywhere — start with subject mastery.

roles.name: Academic Researcher / Professor (research)
roles.description: Produces original research and publishes.
roles.reality: The field's most education for some of its least security.

roles.name: Scientist (industry / lab)
roles.description: Does R&D in a company or institute.
roles.reality: More stable and better-paid than academia.

roles.name: Research Assistant / Lab Technician
roles.description: Supports research hands-on.
roles.reality: A genuine foot-in-the-door into research.
roles.needs: Science degree (bachelor's often enough to start).

roles.name: Social Scientist / Economist
roles.description: Researches human, social, and economic behavior.

roles.name: Data / Computational Researcher
roles.description: Research through data and modeling.
roles.reality: Skills sometimes self-buildable; strong crossover with data science.

roles.name: Librarian / Information Scientist
roles.description: Curates and organizes knowledge and access.

roles.name: Archivist / Curator
roles.description: Preserves records, artifacts, collections.

roles.name: Academic Administrator
roles.description: Runs the operations of schools and universities.

roles.name: Education Policy Specialist
roles.description: Shapes education policy and systems.

families.name: Modern & Accessible Educators
families.blurb: The fast-growing, often self-learnable side of education.

roles.name: EdTech Specialist
roles.description: Builds or runs educational technology.

roles.name: Academic Writer / Science Communicator
roles.description: Explains complex knowledge clearly through writing and media.
roles.reality: Genuinely self-learnable for strong writers.

roles.name: Online Course Creator / Educator
roles.description: Builds and sells courses, teaches to an audience online.
roles.reality: The creator-economy education path — fully accessible, no credential gate.
roles.needs: Expertise + the will to teach publicly.

roles.name: Vocational / Skills Trainer
roles.description: Teaches practical trades and job skills.
roles.reality: Mastery matters more than a teaching degree.
roles.needs: Deep skill in the trade + ability to teach.

roles.name: Academic / Career Counselor
roles.description: Guides students on study and career decisions.
roles.reality: Meaningful, people-centered work.
roles.needs: Counseling/guidance qualification; some entry via experience.

roles.name: Early Childhood / Preschool Educator
roles.description: Teaches and nurtures young children.
roles.reality: Accessible entry, deeply impactful, often underpaid.

roles.name: Translator / Interpreter
roles.description: Converts language across speech or text.
roles.reality: Language-based knowledge work, frequently freelance-friendly.

families.name: Specializations — Where Academia Goes Deep
families.blurb: Niche research, scholarly, and emerging knowledge roles.

roles.name: Bibliometrician / Research Analyst
roles.description: Studies research output and impact itself.

roles.name: Grants / Research Development Officer
roles.description: Wins and manages research funding.

roles.name: Learning Experience (LX) Designer
roles.description: Advanced instructional design for complex learning.

roles.name: Discipline Specialist Researcher
roles.description: Deep expert in a narrow field.

roles.name: Educational Content Developer
roles.description: Creates curriculum and learning materials at scale.

industries.name: Creative, Media & Design Arts
industries.intro: The world of making and storytelling — design, film, animation, music, performance, writing, and media. One of the most portfolio-driven, self-learnable worlds: skill and a body of work open most doors, not degrees. The honest split: some of it is a stable career, some is a calling you fund another way.
industries.one_thing: Making and storytelling. Design and visual, film and video, animation, music and audio, performing, writing, or the media that distributes it all — which form of creating pulls hardest?
industries.wont_give: Stability or, often, good pay early. Much creative work is freelance, project-based, and competitive, and the pure-art paths can be callings you fund with other work. If you need a steady paycheck, the commercial corners (design, marketing) are safer than the fine-art ones.

families.name: Design & Visual Craft
families.blurb: The most employable, stable creative path.

roles.name: Graphic / Visual Designer
roles.description: Designs visual communication — brand, print, digital.
roles.needs: Self-learnable with a strong portfolio; degree optional.

roles.name: UX / UI Designer
roles.description: Designs how products look and feel.

roles.name: Product / Industrial Designer
roles.description: Designs physical products.

roles.name: Interior / Spatial Designer
roles.description: Designs interior spaces.

roles.name: Architect
roles.description: Designs buildings; licensed.
roles.needs: Accredited architecture degree + Council of Architecture registration.

families.name: Film & Video

industries.name: Athletics, Sports & Physical Performance
industries.intro: The world built around the body, competition, and physical excellence — and far larger than 'being an athlete.' The freeing truth: you don't have to be the athlete to live in sport. In India it's exploded beyond cricket-playing into a booming fitness industry, the vast IPL ecosystem, government sport (SAI), and fast-growing sports-tech and fantasy-sports sectors.
industries.one_thing: You don't have to be the athlete. The playing path is a long-shot calling. Build athletes (coaching), heal and optimize bodies (sports medicine and science), or run the business (agency, marketing, data, events)?
industries.wont_give: For the playing path — odds, longevity, security; a calling with a short clock. Elsewhere, much work is insecure (coaching lives by results), modestly paid (fitness, recreation), or brutally competitive (agency, elite medicine).

industries.name: Business, Management & Operations
industries.intro: The world for people who make organizations work — not by building the product or crunching deep finance, but by running the teams, processes, and day-to-day machinery. Its skill set is portable across every industry. In India, the classic doors in are Management Trainee / graduate programs and the MBA accelerator — but plenty of accessible support roles let you start without either.
industries.one_thing: A portable, people-and-process skill set every organization needs. Leading (management), fixing and optimizing (operations), the human side (people, HR), or advising (consulting, analysis)? Often a world you arrive in rather than start in.
industries.wont_give: A single deep craft, or often clear individual credit. Your work is the coordination between specialists, so it can feel intangible — much is responsibility without direct authority, and it can get meeting-heavy and political.
